[Spoiler=Sìway Àñ ]
[b]Weaving contest.[/b]
In  the Garden of Ceibas the intense sound of weaving heard could into the inner if the Sìway Àñ. The day of the cold strings was happening, the contest of the Harem where all women prepare and make their best works for the sapa to wear at the Winter. Seven women, all the  seven Pata Willáy and Kùtái Sao would try their best.
The empress walked in the lines of women weaving, barefoot touching her feet into the well cared and vivid grass, she was carefully watching each work, each was unique, some colored with many geometrical forms, other abstract colors with colors reminiscing the night, others had zoomorphic figures, etc...While the Ñî Chatay, Ñî Chàmpú walked alongside the empress, taking her own phone and posting in the social media of the Imperial Harem the artworks, typing "Absolute master pieces weaven", as herself also commented no much different words admiring the work.
As the Cóya watched, among them, one would be more noticeable, made by a Chûkak Caur of name Élècebetè, she was exception due her weaving abilities to join such contests, her patterns would be in vicugna and guanaco strings dyed to make a what seemed a mountain with a river and the moon at the top, the look in the eyes of the ñîs would be of admiration, and some few other concubines of envy, and fascination. As the empress observed again and again, she stood close to Élècebetè and then touched her shoulders, the servant would look down and stop her working just to wait the empress to speak.
"Taht a very impressive effort is."She then took her hand of the servant in a calm gest of ordering her to continue."Love to see it complete i would, so let it be completed soon."
Élècebetè impressed would be, and a little frozen as she felt the delicate yet "heavy" hands of the empress on her shoulders, but also could not negate the flattery she was feeling. Never she received a direct talking from the Cóya like taht before, so she decided to mutter before backing to weave:
"Thank you, my lady."
As the Ñî Chilla also watched, she looked quite astonished but no less fascinated, as she touched the strings of what seemed a depiction in vicugna wool of the night sky, made by the Pata Willày  Chátí. The art seemed to have even deepth, she questioned it in genuine curiosity:
"May i ask, my dear, ¿what you did to make such technique?"
In a rather happy manner Chátí answered with the following:
"My lady, if you see the position of strings."She pointed as the colors and position of each string"¡You will see the secret behind the technique!""
As the Cóya kept walking observing every work of art, she pointed to the skies and said in a good tall tone:
"Do not forget."Her voice seemed a almost mythical blow"Chatù(goddess of artisans, musicians, artists ...) do not work work with her hands but the land itself. Try to capture her technique into the wool and cotton."
After some time of them observing, they all ended and put their works hanging on the trees of the garden where the Cóya herself would choose. Eventually she passed into a piece which was made of fine guanaco wool with silver so shiny taht could be confounded with the moonlight. None of the concubines were there as this was a private choice for the Ñîs and the empress, she then requested.
"¿Who made this?"
She directed her question to the ladies behind her, lady Chàmpú had her the answer she requested, into a deep reverence she said:
"The Chûkak Caur Élècebetè, my lady."
She answered as soon as the empress replied almost immediately, in a rather contemplative state of the strings while touching softly.
"They all shine in their own manners...they all tell histories and lives in their own ways."She turned her head back finally looking at the Ñîs." ¿Do not you think of it as well?"
The lady of Chilla moved forward with an answer already on her lips with a suggestion.
"The Sapa rules a diverse empire so do you rule this diverse palace my lady.She made a subtle smile ¿why not we unify all those works into a single mantle instead of one for his imperial majesty?"The Cóya then grabbed one of the artpieces and analyzed."The blue of this one shines as the sea..."
Finally the empress taken two of the textiles and put over the polished stone clean ground and instructed:
"Order the other women[servants] to do as i say:
Snip the pieces of green from these textiles from the Kutai Sao, right after fill it with squares of the same to represent his Majesty rule over the sea.she pointed to the star ladies worksThen inside add the black of these to represent night and the little silver strings as the stars, in the middle add the Samán Chilla (lady Chilla) of lady Élècebetè should rest, with the mountains below, and so the river."
She did not said anything, instead her look to the lady Chatay and Chilla said something like "¿do you understand?", the both women nodded in agreement and proceeded to tell the servants.
[/Spoiler]

[spoiler=A City on Fire]Aug 25, 2027

This morning a mass rally was held for the People's Facist Eastornia-Kolionia Party or  PEKP. Those in attendance held up signs with racists and antisemitic signs while chanting racist and antisemitic slogans. When their leader, Hans von Frontent, came up to speak the crowd went wild. Hans's guards struggled to hold back the group of supports trying to push closer to be near their leader. He said very little of much importance, only false and offensive things about Wesserns, Jews, and people of color. At the end of the speech he said probably the only thing worth noting, "We have been oppressed for to long, no we take revenge." That night people broke into loyal Wessernians, Jews, people of color, and others' houses. They looted, they beat the inhabitants, and when they were done they barricaded the doors and set it on fire. It wasn't just houses that were targeted, churches, cathedrals, synagogues, diplomatic and political buildings for Wessern politicians and diplomats, shops, the list goes on and on. Unfortunately what they didn't anticipate was that the fires would spread to neighboring house, and thus the major cities of Kolio, Hanvas, Johuns, Gurtenburg, and others burned well into the night. The worst hit city was the capital of Kolio, the fires turned into a fire storm causing many people to suffocate. The next day Frontent made a speech on a pile of ashes that were once a Wessern's house. He proclaimed, "The Wesserns have done this, in their racist views they have tried to liquidate the entire Kolionian population!" He gestured to the surrounded ruins, "They will pay for their crimes, and we will rule as one Kolionian nation, united under one leader, united under one people. And today is the day that starts."
[/spoiler]
